title: Bencode: Fix 64 bit integers, empty strings and truncated lists
description:
Three independent correctness and robustness bugs in the bencode
dissector, found while working on rtpengine's control protocol but not
specific to it — `packet-bencode.c` is also used by the BitTorrent and
Bazaar dissectors.

### 64 bit integers

The value accumulator was an `int32_t` with no overflow check, so
`i4294967296e` was dissected as `0` and `i2147483648e` as
`-2147483648`. Bencode does not bound its integers, and callers exceed
32 bits routinely — a BitTorrent file length over 2 GiB, or an
rtpengine byte counter in a statistics reply.

Worth noting this was not merely a wrong number: `ival = (ival * 10) +
digit` on a signed 32 bit type is undefined behaviour once it wraps.

The value now accumulates into a `uint64_t`, anything that does not fit
an `int64_t` is rejected rather than wrapped, and `bencode.int` widens
to `FT_INT64`. **That last part is visible to display filters** — the
field changes type, though comparisons keep working.

### The empty string

`0:` is an ordinary bencode string, but the dispatcher only recognised
a length starting `1`-`9`, and a dictionary only looked for a value
once *more than* two bytes were left — which excludes `0:`, `le` and
`de` alike. An empty value therefore aborted the decode of the entire
dictionary containing it.

rtpengine emits them. In one real capture a single empty value cost the
remainder of its dictionary: before the fix, 73 strings dissected and
one "Decode Aborted: Invalid Dictionary Value"; after, 181 strings and
no abort.

### Truncated lists

A list which consumed everything left asked for the remainder of the
tvb, one byte past its end, and threw. `l7:comman` is enough to
reproduce. The dictionary code already handled this correctly; the list
did not.

### Testing

`tshark` built clean; `tools/check_apis.py` and
`tools/check_typed_item_calls.py` report no warnings.

Verified against hand-built payloads covering `INT64_MIN`/`INT64_MAX`,
`INT64_MAX + 1` (correctly rejected), empty strings in first, middle
and last dictionary position, empty lists and dictionaries as values,
and truncated input at every length. Also run over ~20k packets of real
rtpengine traffic with no dissector exceptions.

No capture file is included: the suite has no bencode test today, and
adding one is a larger change than these fixes warrant. Happy to add a
capture-driven test if you would prefer one.

Assisted-by: Claude

commits_data.title: Bencode: Don't run past the end of a truncated list
commits_data.message:
Bencode: Don't run past the end of a truncated list

The dictionary already asks for a zero length item when there is nothing
left to point at, but the list always asked for the remainder of the
tvb - which is one byte past its end once the list has consumed
everything, and threw. "l7:comman" was enough to hit it.

Assisted-by: Claude

commits_data.message:
Bencode: Dissect 64 bit integers

The accumulator was an int32_t and nothing checked it for overflow, so
"i4294967296e" was shown as 0 and "i2147483648e" as -2147483648 - and
"ival = (ival * 10) + digit" on a signed 32 bit type is undefined

Bencode integers are not bounded by the format, and its callers exceed

Accumulate into a uint64_t, refuse anything that does not fit an int64_t
